title: BIM development and documentation for a Swedish family home in ArchiCAD
goal: Develop and improve the BIM model and architectural documentation for a residential building.
context: I work as an architect and regularly use BIM softwares for residential projects. My work includes BIM modeling, architectural documentation, and solving design and technical issues. I chose this task because it represents my typical weekly workflow and allows me to use AI during the design process.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes.I reviewed the existing project, explored the design style with Claude, made several changes to the BIM model, updated the layouts, and published the final layouts as a PDF

Step 1.step_name: Review the existing BIM model and floor plan
Step 1.step_action: Review the existing residential project in 3D and go through the main floor plans. Review the basement, ground floor and first floor and identify areas for improvements or additions.

nodes.label: Open the existing ArchiCAD project
nodes.detail: The user opens 'Svedska kuca - Copy.bpn' in ArchiCAD 28, an existing working file for a Swedish family house (Enbostadshus) with basement, ground floor and first floor already modeled.

nodes.label: Review the ground floor plan
nodes.detail: The user reviews the floor plan, examining rooms to identify areas for improvement before making changes.

Step 2.step_name: Explore the design style with Claude
Step 2.step_action: Ask Claude what design style could be suitable for the Swedish house project. Review examples of contemporary Scandinavian style and consider how these ideas could fit the existing project.

nodes.label: Share the 3D massing model and ask for design recommendations
nodes.detail: The user sends Claude a screenshot of the house's 3D massing model and asks: 'what do you think about this design of the house? Can you give me some design recommendations? What style should I use?'

nodes.label: Critique the massing and propose style directions
nodes.detail: Claude praises the clean two-story massing and full-width deck, but flags the curved gambrel roof as reading more Dutch colonial than Scandinavian, an undefined facade material, inconsistent window rhythm, and minimal roof overhang. It then presents three style directions (contemporary Scandinavian, traditional Falu red, modern minimalist white) as an options card, leaning toward contemporary Scandinavian.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about critiquing the massing and proposing style directions while the generation is ongoing.
Check 3D model
Ask for contemporary Scandinavian reference images
nodes.detail: The user asks: 'Can you give me picture examples of contemporary scandinavian?'

nodes.label: Share Scandinavian reference images and design cues
nodes.detail: Claude searches for and shares photos of black-timber, gable-roofed Scandinavian houses, and calls out translatable cues: crisp roof overhangs with no curved eaves, disciplined window rhythm with full-height glazing at ground level, simple dark-cladding-versus-white-frame material contrast, and low flush decks with minimal railings.

nodes.label: Review the 3D model against the reference images
nodes.detail: The user orbits the 'Generic Perspective' 3D view of the house in ArchiCAD, comparing the existing gambrel roof and blank white massing against the black-timber, gable-roof Scandinavian references Claude shared.

Step 3.step_action: Demonstrate how walls and slabs can be created and adjusted in the residential BIM model. Use the existing house as an example and show how these elements can be modified to support the design.

nodes.label: Ask how to trim walls to the roof
nodes.detail: The user runs into walls that need to be trimmed to the roof and asks Claude: 'How do I trim elements to roof in Archicad? Can you describe it step by step?'

nodes.label: Explain Trim Elements to Roof/Shell and the top-link alternative
nodes.detail: Claude gives step-card instructions for selecting the roof and walls together and running Design > Connect > Trim Elements to Roof/Shell, then explains an alternative associative 'top link' method that keeps walls auto-updating with the roof, plus Solid Element Operations as a manual fallback.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about explaining Trim Elements to Roof/Shell and the top-link alternative
Apply Trim Elements to Roof/Shell in ArchiCAD
nodes.detail: In the 3D view, the user opens the Design menu, selects the roof and walls together, and applies Trim Elements to Roof/Shell.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: e1 asks Claude how to trim elements to the roof in ArchiCAD step by step, and e2 gives the path: select the roof and walls, then Design > Connect > Trim Elements to Roof/Shell. In e4 the user states they will follow this path, then tries a shortcut they know but cannot find the Connect command there, and returns to Claude's route, applying Design > Connect > Trim Elements to Roof/Shell to the roof and walls. The walls are trimmed and the user thanks Claude. Claude's instructions are used as given, so the label is adopt.

nodes.label: Ask for alternative way
Generate an alternative way
Check the 3D model and say they want to make more windows
Ask how to make a chimney
nodes.detail: The user asks: 'How do I make a chimney in Archicad?'

nodes.label: Explain chimney construction methods
nodes.detail: Claude explains building a chimney via a library object or custom-built walls combined with Solid Element Operations to subtract through the roof (and floor slab if needed), noting real chimney height above the roof is governed by regulations tied to pitch and ridge distance.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about chimney construction methods
Change the roof
Ask how to change the material of the roof
Generate the methods to change the material
nodes.detail: Claude explains how to change the roof material through Settings > Model tab > surface field. It suggests searching the surface picker for standing seam, zinc or corrugated metal for a Scandinavian look, and selecting all roof planes together so the change applies uniformly.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about the methods to change the material
Change the color for roof
nodes.detail: The user notes that there's another option to do what Claude provided instructions for and demonstrates that instead.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: e12 asks Claude how to change the material of the roof, and e13 gives the route: roof Settings > Model tab > surface field. The user reads it ('this is one of the options') but says 'the other option is just to do it here' and changes the roof surface another way in ArchiCAD, so Claude's method is not used and the label is reject.

nodes.label: Ask how to change the roof tiles
nodes.detail: The user asks: 'How do I change the roof tiles? I have only one option. Where I can find the surface catalog?'

nodes.label: Suggest the roof Settings dialog and library manager
nodes.detail: Claude explains that having only one surface option usually means the project started from a stripped-down template. It suggests checking for a filter in the Surface picker (Roof Settings > Model tab > Top Surface), importing surfaces through Options > Element Attributes > Attribute Manager, checking the Library Manager for missing libraries, and looking at BIMobject or manufacturer sites for real products. As a last fallback it suggests creating a new surface with an image texture.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about the roof Settings dialog and library manager
Look through the surface catalog without applying a change
nodes.detail: The user opens Options > Element Attributes > Surfaces, searches 'roof', which shows only 'Roof Tiles - French Red', and talks through its properties, then cancels without changing anything.

Step 4.step_name: Develop the exterior elements of the BIM model
Step 4.step_action: Add and develop exterior elements around the house, including the garage, greenery, decking, sunbathing areas and a living hedge. Also demonstrate how to create and adjust the garage roof.

nodes.label: Ask how to add plants and landscaping
nodes.detail: The user asks: 'How to I put plants?'

nodes.label: Explain the Object tool and suggest Swedish species
nodes.detail: Claude explains using the Object tool to search the library for landscaping objects, suggests checking the Library Manager if only a couple of plant options show, and recommends birch (bjork) and pine (tall) for larger trees and rhododendron or boxwood (buxbom) for foundation planting.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about the Object tool and suggest Swedish species
Place trees along the property line
nodes.detail: Using the 'Pine Tree Model 27' object, the user places several pine tree objects along the property boundary at the ground floor, spacing them roughly 5 meters apart, and resizes/repositions a few site elements while reviewing the result in the 3D perspective view. After finishing, the user moves on to the garage space.

nodes.label: Ask about typical garage dimensions
nodes.detail: The user asks: 'What is typical height of the garage?'

nodes.label: Give garage height and door dimension guidelines
nodes.detail: Claude provides a table of typical Swedish garage dimensions: 2.0-2.125m door clear height, 2.4-2.7m interior ceiling height, 2.4-3.0m eave height, and 3.5-4.5m overall ridge height, plus door width guidance for single (2.4-3.0m) versus double (4.8-6.0m) garages.

nodes.label: Build the garage walls, door, and slab
nodes.detail: The user adds a vertical sliding garage door sized for two cars next to the ground floor plan, then builds the garage's walls and a reinforced-concrete slab, working partly in the 3D view to align the new structure with the house.

nodes.label: Create and rebuild the garage roof
nodes.detail: The user creates a new multiplane garage roof at a 30-degree pitch using the Roof tool, and after the initial shape doesn't match the house's gambrel roof form, rebuilds its geometry and re-applies Trim Elements to Roof Shell to clean up the intersections between the garage roof and walls, matching the French-red roof tile finish used on the main house.

nodes.label: Add a deck slab, screening fence and living hedge
nodes.detail: The user sketches a small screening wall/fence near the deck and sunbathing area, draws a deck slab off the kitchen, and places a 'Hedge Model' object along the property boundary to act as a living hedge.

nodes.label: Add deck lounger furniture
nodes.detail: The user places several 'Deck Lounger 01 27' furniture objects on the sun deck in the 3D perspective view, arranging five loungers in a row facing the garden.

nodes.label: Ask Claude about layouts and share the A3 cover sheet
nodes.detail: The user asks: 'How to make a new layout? Can I send you my a3 layout and you tell me if it is ok?' and uploads an image of the layout book's cover/table-of-contents sheet.

nodes.label: Critique the A3 layout and outline new-layout steps
nodes.detail: Claude reviews the cover sheet, noting the empty left two-thirds, missing hero image, disconnected 'PROJEKT: ENBOSTADSHUS' title placement, and centered table-of-contents formatting, then gives step-card instructions for creating a new layout sheet in ArchiCAD's Layout Book.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about critiquing the A3 layout and outlining new-layout steps

Step 5.step_name: Update and publish the architectural layouts
Step 5.step_action: Open the project layouts and update them based on the changes made to the BIM model. Review all layouts and publish the updated layouts as a PDF.

nodes.label: Updates and reviews the layout sheets
nodes.detail: The user navigates the layout sheets page by page, pasting screenshots where missing. They review and update the content to make sure the drawing refects the updated BIM model.

nodes.label: Ask how to export the layouts as a PDF
nodes.detail: The user asks: 'How to I export a pdf in Archicad?'

nodes.label: Recommend using a Publisher Set
nodes.detail: Claude recommends File > Publish for the full drawing set, explaining that saving a reusable 'Publisher Set' lets the user regenerate the whole PDF with one click next time instead of exporting each sheet individually.

nodes.label: Confirm they want to use the Publisher Set
nodes.detail: The user replies: 'I want to use publisher set.'

nodes.label: Walk through Publisher Set configuration
nodes.detail: Claude gives step-card instructions for creating and configuring a Publisher Set: setting the output format to PDF, choosing 'Combine into a single PDF', configuring PDF export options, and ordering the layouts inside the set to match the cover sheet's table of contents before publishing.

nodes.label: Configure and run the Publisher Set
nodes.detail: The user opens the Publisher Set Properties dialog in ArchiCAD, sets the output format to a single combined PDF named 'Swedish House' saved into a new folder on the desktop, and clicks Publish to generate the file.

nodes.label: Verify the published PDF
nodes.detail: The user opens the resulting 'Swedish House.pdf' (14 pages) in the Edge browser and scrolls through it, confirming that the layout sheets, including the updated floor and roof plans, published successfully.
